Dear Pfizer Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the US Medical Affairs Business Operations Lead, HTA, Value & Evidence (HV&E) opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Field Specialist opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. Celina Lin

jobs.title: Operations Specialist - Office Coordinator
jobs.description: About the Team DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We explore robotics and automation to transform last mile logistics in the long term. If you want to work on commercializing autonomy and robotics in a service used by millions of people, then we want to talk to you! About the Role We’re looking for an Operations Specialist - Office Coordinator to own how our DoorDash Labs sites run day to day and to follow every issue through to done. As the tier 2 layer between our front desk and procurement/inventory teams, you’ll triage the request queue, run equipment transport, manage vendor and facilities follow-up, host visitors and events, and coordinate onboarding as the team grows. You’ll work closely with Front Desk, Procurement & Inventory, Workplace, Facilities, Finance, and engineering teams to keep our sites safe, organized, and ready as the team roughly doubles next year. The Operations Specialist - Office Coordinator will report to the Supply Chain Lead. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Own the equipment transport queue (EOS / drones): set priorities, schedule pickups, track every request in Jira, and manage no-shows across sites Triage the daily request queue, making small calls independently and escalating larger decisions (e.g., security, construction, AV) Own tickets and follow-up with Workplace, landlords, and service vendors (cleaning, pest, dumpster, repairs, ServiceChannel), and maintain a weekly open-issues list Walk each site regularly (gate, dumpster, kitchen, restrooms, common areas), log issues, and track corrective work through completion Plan and run hosting: catering orders, demo-day logistics, visitor and event prep, rooms, and shuttles Own the new hire onboarding checklist (desk, badge, access, equipment, orientation) and track desk counts as the team grows Initiate site-level requests (e.g., furniture, desks, cabinets) and hand off to Procurement & Inventory for purchase Take over contractor contract renewals, contractor onboarding, and Coupa processes, including a backlog of contractors expiring at year end Partner with Front Desk, Procurement & Inventory, and Facilities to build repeatable playbooks that can be reused across sites We’re excited about you because… You have 3+ years of experience in office management, facilities coordination, workplace operations, or operations coordination across one or more sites You are highly organized and own follow-through — nothing falls through the cracks until it is closed You have strong communication and interpersonal skills, and are comfortable managing vendors, landlords, and internal stakeholders You can juggle multiple priorities — transport requests, vendor follow-ups, events, and onboarding — in a fast-paced environment, including same-day requests You’re comfortable with everyday operations and procurement systems (Google Workspace, Slack, Jira, Coupa, Brex, ServiceChannel, or similar) You bring sound judgment: you can make small calls independently and know when to escalate larger decisions You bring discretion and a customer-focused mindset to everything you do Nice to Have... Experience in a tech startup or fast-paced corporate environment Experience with Coupa, contractor onboarding, or contract renewals Experience supporting multi-site operations or new site openings Experience planning and running hosted events, demos, or catering Experience supporting hardware, robotics, or R&D teams with inventory or parts handling We expect this position to be filled by 01-09-2027 Compensation Actual compensation within the pay range listed below will be decided based on factors including, but not limited to, skills, prior relevant experience, and specific work location. Base salary is localized according to employee work location. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others. To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here . See below for paid time off details: For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year. For hourly roles: vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week). The national base pay range for this position within the United States, including Illinois and Colorado. $76,900 — $113,000 USD About DoorDash At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods. DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more. Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel. Statement of Non-Discrimination: In keeping with our beliefs and goals, no employee or applicant will face discrimination or harassment based on: race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, age, gender, marital/domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability status, or veteran status. Above and beyond discrimination and harassment based on “protected categories,” we also strive to prevent other subtler forms of inappropriate behavior (i.e., stereotyping) from ever gaining a foothold in our office. Whether blatant or hidden, barriers to success have no place at DoorDash. We value a diverse workforce – people who identify as women, non-binary or gender non-conforming, LGBTQIA+, American Indian or Native Alaskan, Black or African American, Hispanic or Latinx, Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, differently-abled, caretakers and parents, and veterans are strongly encouraged to apply. Thank you to the Level Playing Field Institute for this statement of non-discrimination. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, and any other state or local hiring regulations, we will consider for employment any qualified applicant, including those with arrest and conviction records, in a manner consistent with the applicable regulation. If you need any accommodations, please inform your recruiting contact upon initial connection. Notice Regarding Use of AI and Automated Tools: To streamline our hiring process, DoorDash utilizes an automated recruitment tool called Metaview. How it works: Metaview assists our recruiting team by evaluating job related qualifications and characteristics in connection with hiring. The tool is designed and used to support - rather than replace - human decision-making; trained personnel make final decisions with meaningful human review and oversight, and DoorDash does not use Metaview or other AI-enabled tool in a manner that has the effect of subjecting applicants or employees to discrimination based on any protected characteristic or proxy or for engaging in any protected activity under applicable law. In compliance with New York City Local Law 144, the independent bias audit summary for Metaview is publicly available for review at https://trust.warden-ai.com/metaview/application-review .

Our dynamic team of subject-matter experts comes from diverse backgrounds — including data science, engineering, market research, and consulting — and collaborates to turn data into meaningful insights that have a direct impact on patients’ lives and the future of Pfizer as a data-driven organization. The Sr Analyst, Data Strategy & Management role is a key contributor within the Data Strategy & Management (DSM) team, responsible for executing and operationalizing enterprise data strategy, governance, and foundational data solutions that enable high‑quality analytics and business insights. This role partners closely with senior team members, analytics, data science, and business stakeholders to design, build, and maintain scalable, reliable data assets that support commercial and enterprise decision‑making. The Sr Assoc operates as a hands-on data leader , translating defined strategies and business requirements into well‑engineered, compliant, and reusable data products. This position is ideal for an experienced data professional who thrives in execution, collaboration, and technical problem‑solving, while continuing to grow strategic influence. Collaboration & Stakeholder Partnership Work closely with analytics, marketing, digital, and technology teams to deliver high‑quality data products. Experience translating business requirements into technical data solutions. Working knowledge of data governance, data quality, and compliance concepts. Strong communication and collaboration skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience in commercial, marketing, or regulated environments (e.g., life sciences). Exposure to cloud‑based data platforms and orchestration tools. My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Sr Analyst, Data Strategy & Management – GCA Mexico Analytics Center opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

Best,
Celina Lin

We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. Whether it's flexible work hours, an inclusive culture, or ongoing learning opportunities, we are here to help you thrive and do the best work of your life. You'll run payroll for our US and UK entities and oversee in-country payroll in Mexico and through our EOR partners. This role is hands-on. You’ll run our day-to-day payroll operations while building the processes and automation that let the function scale as we expand. You'll partner closely with People Ops, Accounting, Legal, and Revenue Operations, and you'll be the go-to person for payroll questions across the company. You will leverage AI and automation to streamline payroll workflows, applying strong judgment to determine where human oversight remains critical. YOU WILL: - Build the global payroll function: the documentation, processes, calendars, checklists, SOPs, and controls that let payroll scale with headcount, hire and develop a team as we grow, and lead the payroll side of expanding into new geographies. - Own end-to-end global payroll, including new hires, terminations, salary changes, bonuses, commissions, and leave pay, and act as the escalation point for complex payroll issues and employee pay questions. - Manage our in-country payroll providers and EOR partners across multiple countries, validating inputs and outputs, evaluate the right long-term model for each country, and evaluate payroll tools and providers, recommending what to adopt based on accuracy, cost, and risk. - Own payroll configuration in Rippling and keep payroll data flowing cleanly to the general ledger as we scale, using AI and workflow automation to remove manual work. - Administer deductions and retirement contributions, including 401(k) remittances, and reconcile plan contributions to the plan administrator. - Maintain compliance with payroll taxes, wages, and statutory requirements across the US and the UK, including registrations, filings, year-end reporting, and responses to tax authority notices, and support financial statements, statutory, and 401(k) plan audits with documentation and responses to auditors. - Administer sales commissions and other variable pay with Revenue Operations so plans are paid accurately and on schedule. - Support equity-related payroll processes, including withholding and reporting on exercises and vesting events, in coordination with Legal and Carta. - Partner with Accounting on payroll journal entries, reconciliations, and month-end close, with the goal of bringing payroll accounting into the payroll function over time, and with People Ops on employee lifecycle events (hires, terminations, leaves, and compensation changes) so the data flowing into payroll is accurate. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so. What’s the interview process like? We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process. What if I need accommodations for my interview? At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Product Complaints Analyst 2 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Illumina Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Product Complaints Analyst 2 opportunity with Illumina at Illumina.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Revenue Strategy and Operations , ANZ
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As the Revenue Strategy & Operations partner for Australia and New Zealand, one of our most established markets in Asia-Pacific, you'll work with our ANZ sales leadership to plan and run the business, from the market's largest enterprises and government agencies to its fastest-growing technology companies. You will be the trusted advisor to our sales leaders on how the business is planned and run: where we invest, how we cover the market, and how we read performance in a consumption business, while building the operational foundations to scale. Much of the work you will do yourself, hands-on. This role suits a structured thinker who is comfortable with ambiguity: you will often start from an open question, turn it into a clear recommendation, and get leaders who don't report to you aligned behind it. You'll work closely with Strategy & Operations peers in Singapore, Japan, Korea and India, with global Revenue Operations and Finance, and you'll use Claude every day to do the work of a much larger team. This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll report to the head of Revenue Strategy & Operations for Asia-Pacific, who is also based in Sydney, work day to day alongside our sales leaders and team, and spend regular time with customers and colleagues across Australia and New Zealand. Responsibilities Go-to-Market Strategy Lead annual and quarterly go-to-market planning for Australia and New Zealand with sales leadership and Finance: set targets, territories and sales capacity, and own the trade-offs behind them. Set how we segment the market and design territories across enterprise, public sector, digital natives and startups, and keep books balanced as the team grows. Align leadership on coverage and investment (which industries and accounts get named sellers, what we cover through partners and self-serve), and revisit the call as the business grows. Shape how we go to market with cloud marketplaces, systems integrators and resellers (co-selling, partner pipeline and joint planning), alongside our partnerships team. Give sales leadership an independent read of the business (consumption, pipeline and performance by segment), with the risks, the opportunities and a recommended course of action, early enough to act on. Rhythm of the Business & Regional Leadership Own the operating rhythm for Australia and New Zealand (weekly forecast and pipeline reviews, monthly and quarterly business reviews), and make it the place where decisions get made, not where reports get read. Represent the market with Revenue Operations, Sales Enablement, Finance, Marketing and Partnerships; keep its plans aligned with Asia-Pacific and the company, and bring back what works elsewhere. Advise ANZ and Asia-Pacific leadership through planning sessions, performance reviews and leadership updates. Own the narrative, not just the numbers. Influence without authority: bring structure to ambiguous problems, build the case, and drive decisions across teams you don't manage. Operations & Global Programs Own the market's commercial governance (account and territory decisions, rules of engagement, planning inputs, data standards), working through our global Revenue Operations team, who own the CRM and sales systems. Land global programs, processes and tools in Australia and New Zealand, and be the market's voice back to headquarters when something needs to change. Keep the commercial engine running smoothly across the long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles typical of enterprise and government buyers. You may be a good fit if you have Required qualifications 8-12 years of experience in B2B SaaS, cloud or enterprise software, including several years leading sales strategy, revenue operations or commercial go-to-market work as the advisor to a sales leader, ideally in Australia or New Zealand Structured thinking: a track record of taking ambiguous, open-ended problems and turning them into options, a recommendation and a decision Analytical depth: you can get from raw data to a recommendation yourself, and you know which three numbers a leader needs to see You have owned annual planning, territory design, quota setting and business reviews for enterprise sales teams Hands-on with Salesforce and data (reports, dashboards and your own analysis); you use the systems yourself rather than administer them Presence and judgement with senior sales leadership and C-level stakeholders, including the confidence to give an unwelcome recommendation, and a record of getting decisions made across teams you don't manage Comfortable operating in ambiguity and at pace; you can build the process while running it A record of advising regional leadership on go-to-market strategy and getting the organization behind it Based in Sydney Strong candidates may also have Experience in a consumption or usage-priced business (cloud infrastructure, data or AI platforms): planning and forecasting on usage, not bookings alone Management consulting experience (strategy or operations work), ideally combined with time in an operating role A track record of scaling sales organizations through 3x+ growth periods in B2B software Go-to-market experience with the Australian public sector (federal and state), or with partners and cloud marketplaces in Australia and New Zealand Experience in Chief of Staff or Business Operations roles supporting regional leadership You already use AI tools hands-on in your own work Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.description: TERRITORY: North Indianapolis, IN including Central and North-Central Indiana We’re looking for a dynamic, results-driven Clinical Field Specialist (CFS) to join our growing Women’s Health sales team . This is a high-impact, clinically focused sales role dedicated to driving revenue growth, expanding market adoption, and advancing Natera’s innovative genetic testing solutions. As a CFS, you’ll serve as a trusted clinical and strategic partner to OB/GYNs, Maternal-Fetal Medicine (MFM) specialists, and key healthcare stakeholders , building strong relationships and executing strategic territory plans to accelerate business growth. You’ll combine clinical expertise, consultative selling, and hands-on education to drive adoption of both established and emerging products, influence clinical practices, and ultimately improve patient care. This territory encompasses the northern Indianapolis metropolitan area. Key markets include Carmel, Fishers, Noblesville, Westfield, Lafayette, Kokomo, Anderson, Muncie, Crawfordsville, and Richmond, along with surrounding communities. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES Increasing revenue and driving market development through direct sales to individual MFMs, Ob/Gyns and Genetic Counselors. Sales efforts include effective prospecting, cultivating and maintaining key relationships. Creating and implementing a strategic business plan to grow revenue quickly in your geography. Sales efforts will focus on currently marketed products and new product launches. Will play a critical role in the success of the organization. This role works with PHI on a regular basis both in paper and electronic form and have an access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform the job Employee must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire. Must maintain a current status on Natera training requirements. Beyond OTE, the compensation also features a car allowance and Restricted Stock Units (RSUs). The compensation package listed is for 1st year OTE, which are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Field Specialist — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Field Specialist opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Master Class - Business Consultant - Life Sciences Consulting
jobs.description: Veeva is the industry cloud for Life Sciences. We are enabling agentic biopharma through applications, agents, data, and consulting working together. Learn more about our products, vision, values, and status as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) on our website. Consulting is changing, and Veeva Business Consulting is not like other firms. Launched in 2019, we’ve grown quickly and organically to over 500 global experts who combine deep industry knowledge and unique insights to accelerate drug development and commercialization for our customers. We are growing aggressively and seeking great people to help Life Sciences work in a more efficient and connected way, shaping the future of the industry with the world’s leading AI applications, agents, and data at their back. The Role We are hiring high potential people who are early in their careers and want to pivot into Life Sciences Consulting through our Master Class Program. Breaking into business consulting after starting your career down a different path can be hard. Designed as an alternative to earning an MBA, this program shapes experienced professionals into Business Consultants capable of making an impact for the Life Sciences industry. Business Consulting spans five core practice areas: Analytics, Commercial, Content, R&D, and Quality. As a part of Master Class, you will align to one of those practices, allowing you to build targeted industry expertise. You will be asked to choose your preferred practice in the application process. Early in the program, you will own key workstreams on customer-facing engagements within your practice, creating tailored solutions while collaborating with Veeva team members at all levels. You will be given the tools and resources to accelerate your consulting skills development. If you’re graduating with an advanced degree, have 3-5 years of industry experience, or have served your country and are excited to pivot your career into consulting for a critical industry, Master Class is for you. The anticipated start date is March 2027.

jobs.title: Legal Engineer, Product Specialist
jobs.description: WHY HARVEY At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come. This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started. ROLE OVERVIEW Harvey’s Legal Product Specialists are experienced lawyers from top-tier firms who leverage their legal expertise to help customers seamlessly integrate Harvey into their daily workflows—driving adoption, increasing utilization, and supporting long-term expansion and renewal. Legal Product Specialists collaborate closely with Harvey’s Customer Success Managers and Account Executives to drive all facets of the post-sales strategy. They develop consultative relationships with law firm partners, associates, innovation teams, and in-house counsel at private equity firms and Fortune 500 companies—serving as trusted advisors on how Harvey’s AI solutions can enhance legal effectiveness and efficiency. Legal Product Specialists draw on their legal training and practice experience to ask thoughtful questions, uncover adoption barriers, and develop tailored strategies that build credibility with customers. They partner with Customer Success Managers and Account Executives to communicate Harvey’s value through a mix of large group sessions, small workshops, and one-on-one conversations. You will be the face of Harvey in APAC—building trust with partners and counsel at top firms, corporates, and asset managers; advising them on how Harvey can transform research, drafting, diligence, and compliance; and feeding market insights back to Product and GTM more broadly. cold_email.subject: Interest in Sales Manager, Enterprise - Japan — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear OpenAI Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Sales Manager, Enterprise - Japan opportunity with OpenAI at OpenAI.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: National Security Lead, APAC
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are looking for an experienced National Security practitioner to guide our strategic engagements with Asia-Pacific national security and intelligence communities. Working closely with the national security team based in the US and the APAC policy team, this senior role will help to shape Anthropic's approach to national security policy and partnerships in APAC during a critical period in AI development and governance. You will be the day to day point of contact with national security partners in the Asia-Pacific, translating technological developments for national security audiences and building mutually beneficial collaborations.. You will also work closely with our APAC public sector sales team to support public sector deployment of Claude in high-leverage use cases that strengthen national security, enhance government efficiency, and accelerate allied competitiveness to promote regional peace and security. This role is based in Australia. This job will also require travel across the Asia-Pacific region and to the United States. In this role you will: Lead policy engagement with APAC national security partners on issues related to government use and national security implications of frontier models Engage key NatSec policy stakeholders (e.g., via briefings, consultations, demos, roundtables), in coordination with the wider national security and APAC policy teams. Partner with the APAC public sector sales team to support commercial efforts involving government agency deployments Support and promote public-private research collaborations Build a coalition of government agencies, nonprofits, safety institutes, think tanks and academics to in APAC to share knowledge around national security issues and ensure the safe and responsible adoption of frontier AI Collaborate with technical teams to translate Anthropic threat model research into concrete policy proposals, stakeholder education, and thought leadership opportunities You may be a good fit if you: Have 10+ years of experience working in national security agencies, or a combination of government and related private sector experience Are high-agency, able to develop and execute strategy independently, taking account of dependencies with other cross-functional teams within Anthropic (including but not limited to policy, go-to-market, trust and safety, legal, product, research, comms, and marketing) Possess strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly when briefing policymakers and government officials Have demonstrated interest and experience in a complicated technical subject (ideally, AI, but other examples could be quantum computing, cryptography, fusion power, etc.) Have had some legal training in or exposure to contract negotiation Are willing/able to participate in a process to obtain/retain a security clearance in Australia Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.
